about: Evolution engine tables (ALGORITHM.md sections 4.1 to 4.6). Plain data so the numbers can be tuned without code changes.
coat_patterns_about: E2b: the visible adult coat pattern of each parent, named in prompts as '<animal>-type <pattern>'. An animal not listed has no stripes or spots.

coat_patterns.donkey: dark dorsal stripe and shoulder cross

function_defaults_about: E4: breathing organ and mouthparts for database animals, by class (and by diet for mammal teeth). These are project defaults, marked as such in provenance; learned animals get theirs from Muse Spark (model-estimated). Per-animal overrides are data, not code.

features: three pairs of feathery external gills on the sides of the head

fiction_budget_about: E4, R9 section 3: licenses per design mode (RC-R9-10, RC-R9-11). 'several' for mythic is a product decision (R9 'What this doc does not settle'). 'bendable' is R9 3.2: each license bends one named card and always carries the compensation shown. 'never_licensable' is R9 3.3: honesty rules and the believability floor.

bendable.note: S3c: the respiratory clause comes from the donor's own breathing trait (visible_breathing), never from its phylum. A crab breathes with gills under its carapace, so it shows no flank openings.

bendable.rule: insect wings on a vertebrate body plan
bendable.compensation: insect wings rising from a raised, plated mount between the shoulder blades, with all four legs kept
bendable.note: S2 (E4c): RC-R3-01 and RC-R3-02 cover vertebrate wing donors only. Insect wings are an arthropod part (RC-R3-09 names insect wings) on a vertebrate frame: a body-plan license with a visible dorsal mount. Over budget, the repair drops them.

bendable.compensation: wings rooted in a heavy shoulder structure that can carry them, not floating
a wet habitat or a second, air-breathing system

bendable.rule: tentacles carrying a heavy land body
bendable.compensation: many thick tentacles, short and low to the ground

visible_breathing_about: S3c: what a donor's breathing organ shows on the outside, by its resolved breathing trait. null: nothing visible to draw (gills inside a gill chamber, book lungs under the abdomen, lungs). A value is added to a license compensation only when the donor's own trait names that organ. Source: the donor's breathing provenance (web-cited, model-estimated or project default), recorded on the license.

visible_breathing.tracheae: rows of small breathing openings (spiracles) along the flanks

part_jobs_about: E4, RC-R9-12: the job of each donated part. 'needs' names a habitat condition without which the part has no job ('water': a wet habitat profile). A part with no job is dropped in realistic mode.
routing_about: S2 (ROADMAP 5b): the provider per Spark call type. baseten = Muse Spark Open (meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026, OpenAI-compatible); meta = Muse Spark 1.3 on the Meta API. max_tokens caps a Spark Open answer at about 3x the largest output seen in S1 (reasoning tokens count): identify 1634, checklist 1848, polish 4881, open critic 1185. A failed or cut-off Baseten call falls back to Meta, logged. Plans (the legacy full-plan path), plain and web-cited traits, the function audit and vary stay on Meta (S1: Spark Open runs away on long JSON and trait lists).
critic_decision_about: S3b recalibration (benchmark/calibration_s3b/ITERATIONS.md): on 33 owner-labeled images, Meta Spark 1.3 alone caught 18/18 failures with 3/15 false alarms; Spark Open alone 18/18 with 11/15 (it calls grown pangolin scales on an axolotl 'laid on top' in 8 of the 10 owner-good images); the S3a pair rule (disagreement is a fail signal) inherits Spark Open's false alarms, 11/15. So Meta decides; Spark Open still answers every image and its disagreements are kept on each row as pair_status. Set mode to 'pair' for the S3a rule. Pending owner confirmation.
prosaic_detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin
